dedupe_keys.name: seas5 system4 larsim me seasonal streamflow reforecasts for the german waterways rhine elbe and danube

description: This dataset from the German Federal Institute of Hydrology (BfG) holds seasonal streamflow reforecasts for the German waterways Rhine, Elbe and Danube, produced to evaluate the potential skill of seasonal flow forecasting for navigation. The hydrological model LARSIM-ME, which covers about 800,000 square kilometres of the Rhine, Elbe, Weser/Ems, Odra and Upper Danube catchments on a 5 km grid with a daily time step, was driven by drift corrected reforecasts of ECMWF's Seasonal Forecast System 4 and SEAS5 for 1981 to 2016, started on the first of each month with up to seven months of lead time, and by E-OBS observations for the baseline. It was produced by Bastian Klein and Dennis Meissner in the EU IMPREX project and deposited on Zenodo in March 2020 (version 1.0). Coverage is regional (German waterways). The data are free under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence and available to download as three NetCDF files (System 4, SEAS5 and E-OBS driven flows). Caveats: they are reforecasts for skill assessment, not operational forecasts, and the non-commercial licence limits reuse. They support low-water risk assessment and seasonal planning of inland navigation capacity. They complement the BfG ENS-LARSIM_ME monthly forecasts and are related to the Danube FIS portal water levels.
name: SEAS5/System4-LARSIM_ME seasonal streamflow reforecasts for the German waterways Rhine, Elbe and Danube
